components.title: consent
components.instruction:
Informed Consent

 

Social Media Engagement

This is an invitation to participate in a research study exploring how people view different social media posts. Before you decide whether to participate, it is important that you understand why the research is being conducted and what your involvement will entail. Please take time to read the following information carefully.
Because we use eye-tracking it is IMPORTANT that you remain as still as possible throughout the study (preferably sitting at a desk), keep your face visible to the camera, and avoid leaving your computer until you have completed the study.
 

Study procedure

You will be given different social media posts and asked to answer some questions related to them.

There are no right or wrong answers, your goal is to make honest responses.
 

Type of personal data and when it is deleted/anonymized

We collect both normal and sensitive personal data. All collected data will be anonymized upon finishing the study, ensuring that no identifying information will be recorded.

We do not share your information (e.g., your participant ID or age) with external data processors.

Withdrawal of consent

Participation is voluntary. You may withdraw your consent at any time during the study without providing a reason. Should you decide to stop and withdraw your consent during the study, all responses and your information will be deleted. However, withdrawal of consent after completion of the study is not possible as we cannot identify your data due to anonymization.

components.title: debriefing
components.instruction:
EXPERIMENTAL DEBREIFING INFORMATION
Department of Management
Aarhus University


Name of Experimenters:

Dr. Nick Simonsen (Post-doctoral Researcher; Nick.Simonsen@mgmt.au.dk)

Ms. Lilla Fürtön (Research Assistant; au713732@uni.au.dk)

Prof. Jacob L. Orquin (Professor; jalo@mgmt.au.dk)


Title of Experiment: Can attention be reliably measured using webcam eye-tracking?

Thank you for taking part in this study. During the study, you were asked to read and evaluate a series of social media posts. We are investigating whether webcam-based eye-tracking can be used to meaningfully measure attention in online surveys. Specifically, we are interested in whether patterns of visual attention, as measured through eye movements, remain reliable and stable when people view different images, such as social media posts.

Please continue to the next screen, where you will receive your Prolific completion code and be automatically redirected back to Prolific.
